cover.headline: Slower for good, priced for decline: AI caps TCS's growth but does not justify 12x earnings
cover.lead: TCS is India's largest IT-services company (FY26 revenue ₹2,67,021 cr / US$30,017 m; 25% EBIT margin; ~52% ROE), 71.7% owned by Tata Sons. Its revenue fell 2.4% in constant currency in FY26 as the BSNL contract tapered and clients cut discretionary work, and the stock lost 55% from its 2024 peak as investors concluded that generative and agentic AI will shrink traditional IT services. Our answer to the central question: **both** are true. AI takes 10-15% out of each renewal, so growth will stay well below the 8-10% of the 2010s; but the order book (US$40.7 bn TCV in FY26), new AI work (US$2.6 bn run-rate) and the weak rupee keep earnings growing. We forecast USD revenue +3.3% / +4.2% / +4.8% and EPS of ₹157.2 / ₹167.1 / ₹178.9 for FY27-29E, ~4% above the street in FY28E. The street values TCS on **P/E, 14-15x FY28E**. Our multiple is derived from TCS's 26.0x median forward P/E since 2021, cut by the sector's 29% de-rating (TCS itself is 53% below its median): **18.5x Sep-28E EPS of ₹173.0 gives {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with BUY.** Cross-checks: EV/EBITDA ₹2,975, DCF ₹2,835. Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.p: FY26 CC growth was −2.4%, the widest gap to peers on record; Q1FY27 recovered to +3.2% YoY but only +0.4% QoQ. TCS passes 10-15% productivity to clients at each renewal. We model USD growth of 3.3 / 4.2 / 4.8% for FY27-29E, below the "high single digit" management hopes for once deflation is absorbed.

TCV US$40.7 bn in FY26 with five mega deals, plus the US$800 m+ SKF win in Q1; 66 clients over US$100 m a year (from 62); FY26 EBITDA margin 27% vs Infosys 24%, HCLTech 21%, Wipro 19%; AI services US$2.6 bn annualised, +14% a quarter. TCS is losing hours, not clients.

arguments.h: The rupee and payouts carry the return
arguments.p: FY27E EPS +7.7% on FY26's ₹145.99 adjusted base, almost all from the rupee (₹95.4 vs ₹89.0 per dollar). TCS returns ~90% of earnings: ₹110 a share in FY26, a 5.4% dividend yield at ₹2,051. EPS compounds ~7.0% a year to FY29E.

arguments.h: Valuation: priced as if it were shrinking
arguments.p: At ₹2,051 TCS trades at 12.3x FY28E (its lowest forward P/E in ten years; 26.4x median since 2021), a price consistent with only ~3.4% a year rupee earnings growth forever. Our 18.5x applies only the sector's de-rating; the street's 14-15x and today's price assume TCS deserves a much bigger discount (its own −53% gives 12.2x, about the current price).

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due in October 2026): whether CC growth reaches ~1% QoQ as management's "Q2 better than Q1" implies, and margin climbs from 24.0% towards the 25%+ exit.
AI revenue and deal conversion: the AI run-rate (US$2.6 bn), SKF and UK-telecom ramps, and the BSNL add-on purchase order (final PO awaited in Sep-2026).
Capital allocation: a buyback "remains an option" at a price far below the 2022-23 buybacks (₹4,150-4,500); MHP closing and HyperVault funding.
Rupee and macro: INR ~₹95.8 per dollar on 30-Sep-2026; West Asia conflict, tariffs and US discretionary spending.
AI model launches: the February 2026 sell-off showed how each new agentic-AI release moves IT stocks, whatever the near-term numbers.

sections.title: India's largest IT services firm: US$30 bn of revenue, 594,000 people, 55 countries

blocks.p: TCS builds, runs and changes the technology of large companies. Most of its revenue comes from multi-year contracts to develop and maintain applications, run infrastructure and cloud, implement enterprise software (SAP, Salesforce, Oracle, ServiceNow), test software, secure systems and run back-office processes, with a growing layer of consulting and AI work. It sells by industry: **banks and insurers (BFSI) are 32% of revenue**, consumer businesses (retail, consumer goods, travel) 15.5%, life sciences and healthcare 10.4%, manufacturing 8.8%, technology companies 8.4%, telecoms and media 5.8%, energy and utilities 6%, and "regional markets" (India, public sector, products) 13.1%. By market, **North America is 48.6%**, the UK 17.4%, continental Europe 15.4% and India only 5.9%. About 48.7% of revenue is billed in dollars, 15.1% in pounds and 11.9% in euros (Q1FY27).

sections.title: A low-growth market in the middle of a technology shift

blocks.p: IT services is a ~US$1.5 trillion global market (Gartner, ex-cloud infrastructure) growing ~4-5% a year in dollars. Indian firms win share because they deliver from India at a fraction of onshore cost; the top five (TCS, Infosys, HCLTech, Wipro, Tech Mahindra) earn most of their revenue from US and European banks, retailers, manufacturers and tech firms. Growth comes in waves: the 2021-22 cloud-and-digital boom (TCS +15% in constant currency) was followed by three years of cuts to discretionary projects, and since late 2024 by generative and then agentic AI, which can write code, test software and run IT operations with fewer people. That is good for clients and for whoever builds the new systems, and bad for revenue that is billed by the hour or by the head.

sections.title: Cycle or de-rating? Both, but the price assumes almost no growth

blocks.p: This is the question that decides the stock. TCS fell from ~₹3,190 at the end of January 2026 to ₹2,051 on 30-Sep-2026 (−55% from its 2024 peak), and its one-year-forward P/E from ~20x to ~12x. Two stories explain it. **The cyclical story:** clients have cut discretionary projects for three years, the US-Iran war from late February 2026 and tariffs added uncertainty, and TCS had a company-specific hole: the BSNL network contract, which lifted India to 8.6% of revenue in FY25, tapered in FY26 (India −28.6% in constant currency, ~2.5 points of TCS's −2.4%). **The structural story:** AI lets clients get the same work done with fewer people, so every renewal of an application-maintenance or IT-operations contract is repriced lower, and new money flows to chips, data centres and AI software rather than services.

bullets: **How big is the deflation?** TCS says renewals pass on 10-15% productivity "in most places", spread over a contract's life and usually offset by extra scope. If roughly half its revenue is run-type work renewing every 3-5 years, that is a ~1.5-2.5% a year drag on growth, close to HCLTech's 2-3% estimate for its own book and Kotak's 3.5% base case. It is real and it will last as long as AI keeps improving.

**What offsets it?** AI work (US$2.6 bn run-rate, ~8.5% of revenue, growing ~14% a quarter but lumpy), modernisation of old systems that AI makes cheaper to replace, vendor consolidation (six mega deals in five quarters) and new lines (HyperVault, Salesforce, MHP). Management's own aim for FY27 is to "arrest the degrowth".

**What is cyclical?** BSNL's fall (over by Q2FY26), the consumer and airline weakness tied to the West Asia conflict, and deferred projects that TCS expects to resume. The deal pipeline is intact: TCV US$40.7 bn in FY26 and US$9.5 bn in Q1FY27.

blocks.callout: **Our verdict:** both are true, and the structural part means TCS will not return to the 8-10% dollar growth of the 2010s: we model 3.3% / 4.2% / 4.8% USD growth for FY27-29E. But at ₹2,051 the stock trades at 11.9x our Sep-28E EPS; with a ~52% ROE and an 11.6% cost of equity, that price is consistent with only ~3.4% a year rupee earnings growth forever, i.e. roughly flat dollar earnings once the rupee's drift is counted. That is a de-rating priced as if AI shrinks TCS, not one that merely slows it. We think the market has overshot.

sections.title: Order book: record mega deals, but revenue converts slowly and at lower prices

blocks.p: TCS signed US$40.7 bn of contracts in FY26 (FY25 US$39.4 bn, FY24 US$42.7 bn), ~1.35x a year's revenue, including five mega deals, and US$9.5 bn in Q1FY27 with an US$800 m+ net-new deal from SKF. Roughly half of TCV is renewals and half new programmes (CEO, Apr-2026). The problem is conversion: TCV has stayed at US$39-43 bn a year for three years while revenue went sideways, because renewals carry productivity give-backs and new AI projects are short (12-16 weeks) and must be re-won. Client metrics turned in Q4FY26: every revenue band added clients for the first time in about two years, and the US$100 m+ group went from 62 to 66.

sections.title: Fewer people, more revenue each: AI productivity is already visible

blocks.p: Headcount peaked at 615,318 in Jun-2023 and was 5,84,519 in Mar-2026 after the 2025 restructuring (~12,000 roles, ₹1,388 cr of severance); TCS then added 9,279 people in Q1FY27, the most in over a year. Revenue per employee rose from ~US$46k in FY23 to ~US$50k in FY26. Voluntary attrition is 13.6% (LTM), far below FY22-23's ~17-20%. Wages: FY26 increments were delayed to Sep-2025 and given to ~80% of staff; FY27 increments for all grades from Apr-2026 cost 170 bp of margin in Q1. Subcontracting (fees to external consultants) rose from 4.7% of revenue in Q1FY26 to 5.9% in Q1FY27, a sign of skills TCS does not yet have in-house.

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** TCS has the best cost position and the deepest client relationships in Indian IT, and the balance sheet to keep investing. Those advantages win renewals and consolidation deals, as FY26's mega deals show. But they are advantages of scale in a people-based business, not of technology. When AI lets a client do the same work with fewer people, the moat stops TCS losing the client, not losing the hours. There is no software-like pricing power here; there is a very efficient operator whose market is being repriced.

sections.title: A decade of steady compounding; the last three years were the slowest in TCS's listed history

blocks.p: TCS's revenue grew from ₹1,08,646 cr in FY16 to ₹2,67,021 cr in FY26, 9.4% a year, and net profit from ₹24,338 cr to ₹49,454 cr (7.3% a year, held back by FY26's ₹4,868 cr of one-off charges). The pattern is a post-Covid boom and a long slowdown. In US dollars revenue rose 15.9% in FY22 and 8.6% in FY23, then 4.1%, 3.8% and −0.5% (FY24-26); constant-currency growth was −2.4% in FY26, its second decline in six years (FY21, the Covid year: −0.8%), and this time in a year without a recession. Rupee revenue kept growing (+4.6% in FY26) only because the rupee fell from ~74 to ~89 per dollar over FY21-26.

blocks.p: TCS needs little capital: capex was ₹16,852 cr over FY22-26 (~1.5% of revenue) against operating cash flow of ₹2,27,254 cr. It paid ₹1,64,536 cr in dividends and spent ~₹43,713 cr on buybacks and buyback tax (₹18,000 cr in 2022 at ₹4,500 and ₹17,000 cr in 2023 at ₹4,150 a share: both well above today's price). ROCE rose to 63-65% in FY24-26. Two things are new. In FY26 TCS spent ₹6,770 cr on acquisitions (Coastal Cloud and ListEngage) and agreed to buy MHP from Porsche (EUR320 m EV) in Aug-2026. bullets: **Cash backs profit.** Operating cash flow was 111% of net income in FY26 (TCS basis) and 105% on Screener's (reported profit, after one-offs); over FY15-26 cash from operations (₹4,15,786 cr) was 99% of profit.

**"One-offs" are partly a cost of doing business in the US.** Legal charges of ₹958 cr (FY24, Epic Systems), ₹1,352 cr (FY26, CSC/DXC incl. interest) and ₹668 cr (Q1FY27, CSC again), plus FY26's ₹1,388 cr severance and ₹2,128 cr labour-code charge. We exclude them from forecasts and the forward P/E history (as the street does) but count the legal ones as a real, if irregular, cost.

**Other income is ~6% of pre-tax profit** (₹4,402 cr in FY26 before exceptional items): ₹3,854 cr interest (incl. ₹852 cr on tax refunds, unusual), ₹701 cr investment gains and a −₹611 cr FX loss. TCS also had ₹66,475 cr of FX derivatives outstanding and lost ₹2,771 cr on them in FY26, offset in translation.

**Related parties.** Revenue from Tata group companies ₹7,071 cr (2.6%); brand fee to Tata Sons ₹368 cr; ₹1,500 cr of inter-corporate deposits placed with a Tata Sons subsidiary; FY25 purchases of ₹8,178 cr from Tata group firms were mainly BSNL network equipment from Tejas Networks, passed through revenue at low margin.
**Receivables and goodwill.** Debtor days (incl. unbilled) rose to 93 in FY26 from 67 in FY21; goodwill rose to ₹9,108 cr after the Coastal Cloud and ListEngage deals.

**Disclosure.** Industry and market revenue and CC growth every quarter, TCV, client buckets, headcount and AI revenue; no utilisation or onsite/offshore split any more, and cost categories were restated in Q1FY27.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: GREEN.** Unqualified audit (B S R & Co.; Walker Chandiok proposed from the 2027 AGM), strong cash conversion, no debt. Watch the litigation pattern in the US, receivable days, and how acquired-company revenue is disclosed as M&A picks up.

blocks.p: TCS has no borrowings other than lease liabilities (₹11,283 cr at Mar-26). Goodwill jumped from ₹1,860 cr to ₹9,108 cr with the Salesforce acquisitions. Receivables are the watch item: debtor days (incl. unbilled revenue) rose from 67 in FY21 to 93 in FY26; DSO in dollar terms was 74 days in Q4FY26 and Q1FY27, down from 76 in Q3FY26.

sections.title: Our honest summary: a slower TCS, priced as a shrinking one; BUY at 12.3x FY28E

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** India's largest and most profitable IT-services company (25% EBIT margin, ~52% ROE), with US$40 bn of annual order intake, ~₹38,000 cr of net cash after leases, a 71.7% owner that wants payouts, and a ~90% payout of earnings through dividends and buybacks (₹110 a share in FY26, a 5.4% yield at today's price).

**What you are paying:** 13.0x our FY27E and 12.3x FY28E EPS, the lowest forward multiple in at least ten years, for ~7.0% EPS growth that leans on the rupee. Growth is structurally lower than in the 2010s: AI takes 10-15% out of every renewal and the new AI work is still ~8.5% of revenue. On the street's method, our inputs and the sector de-rating the target is {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): BUY, a valuation call, not a growth call.

**What the market's own de-rating implies:** TCS trades 53% below its five-year median P/E, against 29% for its peers. The market is saying TCS's earnings are more exposed to AI repricing than peers', or will grow more slowly. Applied to our numbers, that discount gives 12.2x Sep-28E EPS, ~₹2,100 a share, about today's price; the midpoint of the two de-ratings (15.3x) gives ~₹2,650. Our 18.5x target assumes TCS de-rates only as much as the sector. If the next few quarters confirm that TCS is losing ground to peers (CC growth below Infosys and HCLTech again in FY27), the own-de-rating level is the right anchor and the stock is fairly priced; the bear case uses it.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Tata Consultancy Services (consolidated, Rs crore). Revenue is built in US dollars by industry vertical (usdBuild below) and converted at a stated INR/USD path; the INR growth that results is entered in revenueGrowth (the authoring script checks that the build sums to model revenue). TCS reports an operating (EBIT) margin after depreciation; the engine's EBITDA margin = our EBIT margin + engine depreciation / revenue. Forecasts are before exceptional items (the Q1FY27 Rs668 cr CSC charge is left out, as the street does). Net Profit on Screener includes minorities (~0.5%); the engine's share count (363.6 cr) is inflated by the same ratio, so EPS is on the attributable basis. Valued on P/E, as the street does.

usdBuild._why: USD growth, cross-currency held flat (Q1FY27 GBP/USD 1.34, EUR/USD 1.16). FY27E +3.3%: Q1FY27 US$7,624 m annualised is already +1.6% on FY26; we add ~1% QoQ in Q2-Q3 (management: Q2 'better than' Q1; TCV US$9.5 bn in Q1 and US$40.7 bn in FY26) and a weaker Q4, plus a partial BSNL add-on ramp in H2 (Regional Markets +5.5%) and three extra quarters of Coastal Cloud. By vertical: BFSI +3.8% (Q1 run-rate +1.9%, 'good growth across geographies'); Consumer -1.5% (large projects ended in Q1, airlines and discretionary retail weak); LSH +2.5% (declined in Q1, recovery 'expected soon'); Manufacturing +4% (SKF US$800 m over five years ramps from H2); Technology +5% (Q1 run-rate +2.8%, growing ~1.5% QoQ); CMI +2%; ERU +7% (Q1 run-rate +6.7%). FY28E +4.2% and FY29E +4.7%: AI work (US$2.6 bn run-rate, ~8.5% of revenue, +13.6% QoQ) and mega-deal ramps outgrow 2-3% a year of productivity pass-through on the legacy book (TCS: 10-15% over a contract's life; HCLTech: 2-3% a year). Below management's 'high single digit once deflation is absorbed' and in line with the street (MOSL USD +2.2%/+3.0%, ICICI Direct +2.5%/+3.4%, PL CC +3.5%/+4.5%). HyperVault (data centres) and MHP (Porsche consulting, EUR320 m EV, announced Aug-2026) revenue are not included.
usdBuild._fxWhy: INR/USD (TCS's effective rate = INR revenue / USD revenue): FY26 88.96; Q1FY27 94.80; 30-Sep-2026 close ~95.83 (5paisa). FY27E 95.44 = Q1 actual, Q2 ~95.3 and H2 at the 30-Sep spot. FY28E-29E: 1.5% a year depreciation (the rupee fell ~3% a year over FY16-26). Each 1% on the rupee moves revenue ~1% and EBIT margin ~20-30 bp (Q4FY26: ~110 bp on a 3.8% move; Q1FY27: 40 bp on 2.2%), ~2% of EPS; TCS hedges part of its exposure.

assumptions._marginWhy: EBIT (TCS operating) margin 24.6% / 25.0% / 25.2% plus engine depreciation of ~1.7-1.8% of revenue. FY27E 24.6%: Q1 24.0% after the 170 bp wage hit; management wants to 'exit at 25% plus' (Q1 call), so ~24.4/24.8/25.1% in Q2-Q4. FY28E 25.0% = FY26's four-year high: utilisation and pyramid gains, the 1.5% rupee tailwind and AI revenue at higher revenue productivity, offset by continued investment (partnerships, GTM, acquisitions) and renewal pricing. FY29E 25.2%: a step towards the 'move towards 26%, on a longer-term basis' (CFO, Apr-2026). Street FY28E EBIT: MOSL 25.0%, ICICI Direct 24.8%, Choice 24.0%. Depreciation on TCS's share of HyperVault capex sits inside these margins (no HyperVault revenue modelled), a small conservative bias.
assumptions._capexWhy: Core IT capex Rs4,500 / 4,700 / 4,900 cr (Screener cash-flow basis: Rs3,937 cr FY25, Rs4,146 cr FY26; IFRS Rs4,885 cr FY26; Q1FY27 Rs750 cr) plus Rs3,000 cr a year for TCS's 51% share of the up-to-Rs18,000 cr HyperVault programme with TPG (~Rs9,200 cr over FY27-29E). Consolidated capex will be higher (TPG's 49% and project debt) but the engine has no minority or project-debt line, so we model TCS's economic share. MHP's EUR320 m (~Rs3,550 cr) is not included.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs5,560 cr = 9.8% of average gross block (Rs56,147 cr; gross block includes Rs9,108 cr of goodwill that is not amortised); Q1FY27 Rs1,239 cr (~Rs4,960 cr annualised) after acquired intangibles ran off (other intangibles Rs940 cr to Rs176 cr in FY26). 7.6% gives Rs4,900 cr in FY27E, rising to ~Rs6,070 cr in FY29E as HyperVault capex is depreciated at once (engine limit: CWIP held flat).

otherTreasury._why: Inter-corporate deposits of Rs1,500 cr (max 24 months) and Rs900 cr of overnight reverse repo at Mar-26 sit in 'loans' (AR FY26 note 8(e)), i.e. inside Screener's other assets. With Screener cash (Rs12,908 cr) and investments (Rs33,988 cr) they make Rs49,296 cr of the Rs50,020 cr 'invested funds' TCS reports.

assumptions._treasuryWhy: Applied to net cash: cash + investments + ICDs - lease liabilities (Rs11,283 cr; TCS has no other debt) = Rs38,013 cr at Mar-26. FY26 recurring treasury income (interest on deposits Rs726 cr + amortised-cost Rs217 cr + FVOCI bonds Rs2,059 cr + dividends Rs35 cr + FVTPL gains Rs368 cr = Rs3,405 cr) was 7.0% of average invested funds (Rs48,621 cr; AR FY26 note 13). Indian bond yields were lower in 2026 than in FY25; we hold 7.0%.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Non-treasury and gross-up items: (1) 7.0% on the slice of invested funds that offsets lease liabilities (treasury income is earned on gross funds, but the engine applies the yield to net cash): ~Rs790 / 830 / 870 cr; (2) recurring other items (interest on tax refunds at a normal level, rent, lease-modification gains) ~Rs200 cr; (3) FY27E only: Rs655 cr by which Q1FY27's actual gross other income (Rs1,568 cr = Rs1,295 cr net + Rs273 cr finance costs; composition not disclosed quarterly) exceeded our quarterly run-rate. FY27E total other income ~Rs4,310 cr = TTM to Jun-26 before exceptional items (Rs4,310 cr) and FY26 (Rs4,402 cr). FY28E falls to ~Rs3.7k cr because FY26 and Q1FY27 carried items we do not repeat: Rs852 cr interest on tax refunds, Rs333 cr gains on selling FVOCI bonds and Rs191 cr litigation awards, partly offset by a Rs611 cr FX loss (AR FY26 note 13).
assumptions._interestLabel: Finance costs (lease interest; FY27E incl. Rs69 cr on the CSC judgement)
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 Rs1,227 cr = lease interest Rs778 cr + other Rs440 cr (incl. Rs342 cr on the CSC judgement). Q1FY27 Rs273 cr incl. ~Rs69 cr CSC interest. Leases grow with new offices (right-of-use assets +19% in FY26).
assumptions._taxWhy: FY26 effective tax rate 24.6% before exceptional items (CFO); Q1FY27 25.2% (Rs4,692 cr on Rs18,612 cr). Minorities are not in the tax line: the engine's share count already carries Screener's minority ratio.
assumptions._payoutWhy: TCS returns 'substantial' free cash flow: dividends were 100% of EPS in FY23, 58% in FY24 (+ a Rs17,000 cr buyback, ~95% in total), 94% in FY25 and 81% of reported EPS in FY26 (Rs110). We use 90% of EPS as dividends and buybacks combined (the engine cannot cut the share count, so a buyback is treated as a dividend; EPS would be ~0.5-1% higher a year if part were a buyback).

dcf._betaWhy: Net cash, the largest and most diversified Indian IT exporter; but AI substitution risk to its business model is a real uncertainty, so we do not go below 0.85 (Ke 11.6%).
dcf._tgWhy: In rupees: ~3-3.5% long-run USD growth for a mature IT-services book plus ~1.5-2% rupee depreciation. Below the house 5-6% range's top because AI deflation may cap the industry's long-run growth.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: INR revenue growth fades from ~6.3% (FY29E) to 5.5% over 15 years.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: EBITDA margin ~27.0% in FY29E (EBIT ~25.2%) eases to 26.5% (EBIT ~24.7%): pricing pressure on renewals offsets rupee tailwinds.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex falls from ~2.4% of revenue (with HyperVault equity) to 2.0% (TCS's history: 1.5-2%).

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Discretionary spending recovers in 2027 and AI turns net accretive faster: AI work (US$2.6 bn run-rate) keeps growing 40-50% a year, mega deals ramp, CC growth reaches 5-6% by FY28-29 (the 'high single digit' management talks about is in sight) and EBIT margin moves to 25.5-26%.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: AI deflation wins: productivity pass-through of 3-5% a year on the legacy book (the high end of HCLTech's industry estimate) outruns AI revenue, renewals reprice lower and clients move spend to GCCs and AI software. USD growth stays at 1-2%, the rupee stops depreciating and EBIT margin slips to ~23.5-24%.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values TCS: every broker that discloses a method uses P/E, mostly 14-15x FY28E after Q1FY27 (MOSL and PL 15x, ICICI Direct 14x, 360 ONE 14x, Antique 14x 1HFY29E, Emkay 16x Jun-28E, Nuvama 18x, BOBCAPS 12.7x, Nirmal Bang 12x; Jul-2026). Derived on the library rule (sector de-rating only): (1) TCS's median one-year-forward P/E since Apr-2021 is 26.4x (forwardMedian, no trough years) or 26.0x on EPS before the FY24 and FY26 one-offs (used); (2) the eight IT-services peers of the batch set traded a median 29.0% below their five-year median P/E on 30-Sep-2026 (Infosys -49%, Wipro -40%, LTM -38%, LTTS -31%, Mphasis -27%, HCLTech -21%, Persistent -18%, Coforge -11%; TCS and Tech Mahindra excluded) = 26.0x x 0.71 = 18.5x. Sensitivities, not the base: incumbents only (-39.9%) 15.6x; TCS's own -53% de-rating 12.2x; their midpoint 15.3x. Growth and returns check: a Gordon-growth P/E at an 11.6% cost of equity and a 52% ROE is 14.4x for 5% and 16.8x for 6% long-run growth; 18.5x needs ~6.5% (our FY26-29E EPS growth ~7%, FY21-26 10.7%). Bull 22x (TCS's 25th-percentile forward P/E since Apr-2021, 21.9x); bear 12x (TCS's own de-rating level, 12.2x, and its lowest forward P/E since 2016, 12.4x in Sep-2026).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Counts net cash at face value. TCS's median trailing EV/EBITDA since Apr-2021 is 20.2x; the same sector de-rating (-29.0%) gives 14.3x trailing, restated for Sep-28E EBITDA being ~17% above the twelve months to Jun-26 (Rs74,079 cr) = 12.2x, rounded to 12x. Bull 14x and bear 8x scale with the P/E cases (bear = TCS's own 52% EV/EBITDA de-rating, 9.6x trailing, restated).
